# zgbsvx

> Solves a complex system A*X = B where A is general band, with equilibration, condition estimation, and error bounds.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zgbsvx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zgbsvx';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zgbsvx(
    order,
    fact, trans,
    N, kl, ku, nrhs,
    AB, LDAB,
    AFB, LDAFB,
    IPIV, strideIPIV,
    equed,
    r, strideR,
    c, strideC,
    B, LDB,
    X, LDX,
    rcond,
    FERR, strideFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR,
    WORK,
    RWORK
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `fact` | `"not-factored" \| "equilibrate" \| "factored"` | Specifies whether or not the factored form of the matrix A is supplied on entry, and if not, whether the matrix A should be equilibrated before it is factored. `'factored'`: On entry, AFB and IPIV contain the factored form of A. If `equed !== 'none'`, the matrix A has been equilibrated with scaling factors given by R and C. AB, AFB, and IPIV are not modified. `'not-factored'`: The matrix A will be copied to AFB and factored. `'equilibrate'`: The matrix A will be equilibrated if necessary, then copied to AFB and factored. |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | Specifies the form of the system of equations. `'no-transpose'`: A \* X = B (No transpose) `'transpose'`: A\*\*T \* X = B (Transpose) `'conjugate-transpose'`: A\*\*H \* X = B (Conjugate transpose) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A.<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `kl` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of subdiagonals within the band of A.<br>Requires `kl ≥ 0` |
| `ku` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of superdiagonals within the band of A.<br>Requires `ku ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X.<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>(kl + ku + 1) × N</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, the matrix A in band storage, in rows 1 to KL+KU+1. On exit, if `equed !== 'none'`, A is scaled as follows: `equed === 'row'`: A := diag(R) \* A `equed === 'column'`: A := A \* diag(C) `equed === 'both'`: A := diag(R) \* A \* diag(C). |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `AB`<br>Column-major requires `LDAB ≥ kl + ku + 1`<br>Row-major requires `LDAB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `AFB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>(2 * kl + ku + 1) × N</sub> | **in/out** · If `fact === 'factored'`, then AFB is an input argument and on entry contains details of the LU factorization of the band matrix A, as computed by ZGBTRF. |
| ↳ `LDAFB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `AFB`<br>Column-major requires `LDAFB ≥ 2 * kl + ku + 1`<br>Row-major requires `LDAFB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · If `fact === 'factored'`, then IPIV is an input argument and on entry contains the pivot indices from the factorization A = L\*U as computed by ZGBTRF; row i of the matrix was interchanged with row IPIV(i) (0-based). |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride length for `IPIV` |
| `equed` | `Array.<string>` | **in/out** · Specifies the form of equilibration that was done. `'none'`: No equilibration (always true if `fact === 'not-factored'`). `'row'`: Row equilibration, i.e., A has been premultiplied by diag(R). `'column'`: Column equilibration, i.e., A has been postmultiplied by diag(C). `'both'`: Both row and column equilibration, i.e., A has been replaced by diag(R) \* A \* diag(C). EQUED is an input argument if `fact === 'factored'`; otherwise, it is an output argument.<br>Rejects `fact === 'factored' && !(((equed === 'row' \|\| equed === 'both') \|\| (equed === 'column' \|\| equed === 'both')) \|\| equed === 'none')` |
| `r` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · The row scale factors for A. |
| ↳ `strideR` | `integer` | Stride length for `r` |
| `c` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · The column scale factors for A. |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | Stride length for `c` |
| `B` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, the right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `equed === 'none'`, B is not modified; if `trans === 'no-transpose'` and `equed === 'row'` or `equed === 'both'`, B is overwritten by diag(R)\*B; if `trans === 'transpose'` or `trans === 'conjugate-transpose'` and `equed === 'column'` or `equed === 'both'`, B is overwritten by diag(C)\*B. |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `B`<br>Column-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, N)`<br>Row-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, nrhs)` |
| `X` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **out** · If INFO = 0 or INFO = N+1, the N-by-NRHS solution matrix X to the original system of equations. |
| ↳ `LDX` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `X`<br>Column-major requires `LDX ≥ max(1, N)`<br>Row-major requires `LDX ≥ max(1, nrhs)` |
| `rcond` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the matrix A after equilibration (if done) |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nrhs</sub> | **out** · The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector X(j) (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | Stride length for `FERR` |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nrhs</sub> | **out** · The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector X(j) (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes X(j) an exact solution). |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | Stride length for `BERR` |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 2 * N</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided workspace of at least `2 * N` elements |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, N)</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided workspace of at least `max( 1, N )` elements |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `fact`: Specifies whether or not the factored form of the matrix A is supplied on entry, and if not, whether the matrix A should be equilibrated before it is factored.

  -   `= 'F'`: On entry, `AFB` and `IPIV` contain the factored form of A.  If `EQUED` is not 'N', the matrix A has been equilibrated with scaling factors given by R and C. `AB`, `AFB`, and `IPIV` are not modified.
  -   `= 'N'`: The matrix A will be copied to `AFB` and factored.
  -   `= 'E'`: The matrix A will be equilibrated if necessary, then copied to `AFB` and factored.
- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations.

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose)
- `N`: The number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kl`: The number of subdiagonals within the band of A. $\mathrm{KL} \ge 0$.
- `ku`: The number of superdiagonals within the band of A. $\mathrm{KU} \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: On entry, the matrix A in band storage, in rows 1 to `KL`+`KU`+1. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: `AB(KU+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{KU}) \le i \le \min (N,j+\mathrm{kl})$

  If `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED` is not 'N', then A must have been equilibrated by the scaling factors in R and/or C. `AB` is not modified if `FACT = 'F'` or 'N', or if `FACT = 'E'` and `EQUED = 'N'` on exit.

  On exit, if $\mathrm{EQUED} \ne \text{'N'}$, A is scaled as follows: `EQUED = 'R'`: A := $\operatorname{diag}(R) \, A$ `EQUED = 'C'`: A := $A \, \operatorname{diag}(C)$ `EQUED = 'B'`: A := $\operatorname{diag}(R) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(C)$.
- `AFB`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `AFB` is an input argument and on entry contains details of the LU factorization of the band matrix A, as computed by ZGBTRF. U is stored as an upper triangular band matrix with `KL`+`KU` superdiagonals in rows 1 to `KL`+`KU`+1, and the multipliers used during the factorization are stored in rows `KL`+`KU`+2 to $2 \, \mathrm{KL}+\mathrm{KU}+1$. If $\mathrm{EQUED} \ne \text{'N'}$, then `AFB` is the factored form of the equilibrated matrix A.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `AFB` is an output argument and on exit returns details of the LU factorization of A.

  If `FACT = 'E'`, then `AFB` is an output argument and on exit returns details of the LU factorization of the equilibrated matrix A (see the description of `AB` for the form of the equilibrated matrix).
- `IPIV`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `IPIV` is an input argument and on entry contains the pivot indices from the factorization $A = L \, U$ as computed by ZGBTRF; row i of the matrix was interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `IPIV` is an output argument and on exit contains the pivot indices from the factorization $A = L \, U$ of the original matrix A.

  If `FACT = 'E'`, then `IPIV` is an output argument and on exit contains the pivot indices from the factorization $A = L \, U$ of the equilibrated matrix A.
- `equed`: Specifies the form of equilibration that was done.

  -   `= 'N'`: No equilibration (always true if `FACT = 'N'`).
  -   `= 'R'`: Row equilibration, i.e., A has been premultiplied by diag(R).
  -   `= 'C'`: Column equilibration, i.e., A has been postmultiplied by diag(C).
  -   `= 'B'`: Both row and column equilibration, i.e., A has been replaced by $\operatorname{diag}(R) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(C)$. `EQUED` is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, it is an output argument.
- `r`: The row scale factors for A. If `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B', A is multiplied on the left by diag(R); if `EQUED = 'N'` or 'C', R is not accessed. R is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, R is an output argument. If `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B', each element of R must be positive.
- `c`: The column scale factors for A. If `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', A is multiplied on the right by diag(C); if `EQUED = 'N'` or 'R', C is not accessed. C is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, C is an output argument. If `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', each element of C must be positive.
- `B`: On entry, the right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `EQUED = 'N'`, B is not modified; if `TRANS = 'N'` and `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B', B is overwritten by $\operatorname{diag}(R) \, B$; if `TRANS = 'T'` or 'C' and `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', B is overwritten by $\operatorname{diag}(C) \, B$.
- `X`: If `INFO = 0` or $\mathrm{INFO} = N+1$, the N-by-`NRHS` solution matrix X to the original system of equations. Note that A and B are modified on exit if $\mathrm{EQUED} \ne \text{'N'}$, and the solution to the equilibrated system is $\operatorname{inv}(\operatorname{diag}(C)) \, X$ if `TRANS = 'N'` and `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', or $\operatorname{inv}(\operatorname{diag}(R)) \, X$ if `TRANS = 'T'` or 'C' and `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B'.
- `rcond`: The estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the matrix A after equilibration (if done). If `RCOND` is less than the machine precision (in particular, if `RCOND = 0`), the matrix is singular to working precision. This condition is indicated by a return code of $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for `RCOND`, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).
- `RWORK`: On exit, `RWORK(1)` contains the reciprocal pivot growth factor norm(A)/norm(U). The "max absolute element" norm is used. If `RWORK(1)` is much less than 1, then the stability of the LU factorization of the (equilibrated) matrix A could be poor. This also means that the solution X, condition estimator `RCOND`, and forward error bound `FERR` could be unreliable. If factorization fails with $0<\mathrm{INFO} \le N$, then `RWORK(1)` contains the reciprocal pivot growth factor for the leading `INFO` columns of A.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (INFO)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "equilibrate", "factored", "not-factored"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `kl + ku + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `2 * kl + ku + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `TypeError` fourteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `fact === "factored" && !( ( ( equed[ 0 ] === "row" \|\| equed[ 0 ] === "both" ) \|\| ( equed[ 0 ] === "column" \|\| equed[ 0 ] === "both" ) ) \|\| equed[ 0 ] === "none" )`)
- `RangeError` twentieth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` twentieth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-second argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-second argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zgbsvx.strided(
    fact, trans,
    N, kl, ku, nrhs,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    AFB, strideAFB1, strideAFB2, offsetAFB,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    equed,
    r, strideR, offsetR,
    c, strideC, offsetC,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    X, strideX1, strideX2, offsetX,
    rcond,
    FERR, strideFERR, offsetFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR, offsetBERR,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork
) → integer
```

Expert driver for solving a complex system of linear equations A*X = B.
where A is a general band matrix with KL subdiagonals and KU superdiagonals.

Provides equilibration, condition estimation, iterative refinement, and
error bounds.

FACT controls whether to factor, equilibrate+factor, or use pre-factored:
  'not-factored' - factor A, no equilibration
  'equilibrate'  - equilibrate if needed, then factor
  'factored'     - use pre-factored AFB and IPIV (and pre-computed R,C if equilibrated)

TRANS specifies the system:
  'no-transpose'         - A _ X = B
_   'transpose'            - A^T _ X = B
  'conjugate-transpose'  - A^H * X = B

EQUED (input if FACT='factored', output otherwise):
  'none'   - no equilibration
  'row'    - row equilibration (A premultiplied by diag(R))
  'column' - column equilibration (A postmultiplied by diag(C))
  'both'   - both row and column equilibration

Returns { info, equed, rcond, rpvgrw } where:
  info: 0=success, i (1-based)=U(i,i) is zero, N+1=singular to working precision
  equed: equilibration type applied
  rcond: reciprocal condition number estimate
  rpvgrw: reciprocal pivot growth factor

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fact` | `"not-factored" \| "equilibrate" \| "factored"` | 'not-factored', 'equilibrate', or 'factored' |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | 'no-transpose', 'transpose', or 'conjugate-transpose' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `kl` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of subdiagonals<br>Requires `kl ≥ 0` |
| `ku` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of superdiagonals<br>Requires `ku ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of right-hand side columns<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>(kl + ku + 1) × N</sub> | **in/out** · Band matrix in band storage ((KL+KU+1) x N) |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | Stride of first dimension of AB (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | Stride of second dimension of AB (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for AB (complex elements) |
| `AFB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>(2 * kl + ku + 1) × N</sub> | **in/out** · Factored band matrix ((2\*KL+KU+1) x N, output) |
| ↳ `strideAFB1` | `integer` | Stride of first dimension of AFB (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideAFB2` | `integer` | Stride of second dimension of AFB (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetAFB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for AFB (complex elements) |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Pivot indices (0-based, output) |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride for IPIV |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for IPIV |
| `equed` | `Array.<string>` | **in/out** · Equilibration type (input if FACT='factored')<br>Rejects `fact === 'factored' && !(((equed === 'row' \|\| equed === 'both') \|\| (equed === 'column' \|\| equed === 'both')) \|\| equed === 'none')` |
| `r` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Row scale factors |
| ↳ `strideR` | `integer` | Stride for r |
| ↳ `offsetR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for r |
| `c` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Column scale factors |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | Stride for c |
| ↳ `offsetC` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for c |
| `B` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · N-by-NRHS right-hand side (may be scaled on exit) |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of first dimension of B (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of second dimension of B (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for B (complex elements) |
| `X` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **out** · N-by-NRHS solution matrix (output) |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | Stride of first dimension of X (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | Stride of second dimension of X (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for X (complex elements) |
| `rcond` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the matrix A after equilibration (if done) |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nrhs</sub> | **out** · Forward error bounds (output, length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | Stride for FERR |
| ↳ `offsetFERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for FERR |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nrhs</sub> | **out** · Backward error bounds (output, length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | Stride for BERR |
| ↳ `offsetBERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for BERR |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 2 * N</sub> | **out** · Complex workspace (length >= 2\*N) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for WORK (complex elements) |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, N)</sub> | **out** · Real workspace (length >= N) |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | Stride for RWORK |
| ↳ `offsetRWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for RWORK |

<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `fact`: Specifies whether or not the factored form of the matrix A is supplied on entry, and if not, whether the matrix A should be equilibrated before it is factored.

  -   `= 'F'`: On entry, `AFB` and `IPIV` contain the factored form of A.  If `EQUED` is not 'N', the matrix A has been equilibrated with scaling factors given by R and C. `AB`, `AFB`, and `IPIV` are not modified.
  -   `= 'N'`: The matrix A will be copied to `AFB` and factored.
  -   `= 'E'`: The matrix A will be equilibrated if necessary, then copied to `AFB` and factored.
- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations.

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose)
- `N`: The number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kl`: The number of subdiagonals within the band of A. $\mathrm{KL} \ge 0$.
- `ku`: The number of superdiagonals within the band of A. $\mathrm{KU} \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.

  If `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED` is not 'N', then A must have been equilibrated by the scaling factors in R and/or C. `AB` is not modified if `FACT = 'F'` or 'N', or if `FACT = 'E'` and `EQUED = 'N'` on exit.

- `AFB`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `AFB` is an input argument and on entry contains details of the LU factorization of the band matrix A, as computed by ZGBTRF. U is stored as an upper triangular band matrix with `KL`+`KU` superdiagonals in rows 1 to `KL`+`KU`+1, and the multipliers used during the factorization are stored in rows `KL`+`KU`+2 to $2 \, \mathrm{KL}+\mathrm{KU}+1$. If $\mathrm{EQUED} \ne \text{'N'}$, then `AFB` is the factored form of the equilibrated matrix A.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `AFB` is an output argument and on exit returns details of the LU factorization of A.

  If `FACT = 'E'`, then `AFB` is an output argument and on exit returns details of the LU factorization of the equilibrated matrix A (see the description of `AB` for the form of the equilibrated matrix).
- `IPIV`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `IPIV` is an input argument and on entry contains the pivot indices from the factorization $A = L \, U$ as computed by ZGBTRF; row i of the matrix was interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `IPIV` is an output argument and on exit contains the pivot indices from the factorization $A = L \, U$ of the original matrix A.

  If `FACT = 'E'`, then `IPIV` is an output argument and on exit contains the pivot indices from the factorization $A = L \, U$ of the equilibrated matrix A.
- `equed`: Specifies the form of equilibration that was done.

  -   `= 'N'`: No equilibration (always true if `FACT = 'N'`).
  -   `= 'R'`: Row equilibration, i.e., A has been premultiplied by diag(R).
  -   `= 'C'`: Column equilibration, i.e., A has been postmultiplied by diag(C).
  -   `= 'B'`: Both row and column equilibration, i.e., A has been replaced by $\operatorname{diag}(R) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(C)$. `EQUED` is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, it is an output argument.
- `r`: The row scale factors for A. If `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B', A is multiplied on the left by diag(R); if `EQUED = 'N'` or 'C', R is not accessed. R is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, R is an output argument. If `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B', each element of R must be positive.
- `c`: The column scale factors for A. If `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', A is multiplied on the right by diag(C); if `EQUED = 'N'` or 'R', C is not accessed. C is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, C is an output argument. If `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', each element of C must be positive.
- `B`: On entry, the right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `EQUED = 'N'`, B is not modified; if `TRANS = 'N'` and `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B', B is overwritten by $\operatorname{diag}(R) \, B$; if `TRANS = 'T'` or 'C' and `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', B is overwritten by $\operatorname{diag}(C) \, B$.
- `X`: If `INFO = 0` or $\mathrm{INFO} = N+1$, the N-by-`NRHS` solution matrix X to the original system of equations. Note that A and B are modified on exit if $\mathrm{EQUED} \ne \text{'N'}$, and the solution to the equilibrated system is $\operatorname{inv}(\operatorname{diag}(C)) \, X$ if `TRANS = 'N'` and `EQUED = 'C'` or 'B', or $\operatorname{inv}(\operatorname{diag}(R)) \, X$ if `TRANS = 'T'` or 'C' and `EQUED = 'R'` or 'B'.
- `rcond`: The estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the matrix A after equilibration (if done). If `RCOND` is less than the machine precision (in particular, if `RCOND = 0`), the matrix is singular to working precision. This condition is indicated by a return code of $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for `RCOND`, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).
- `RWORK`: On exit, `RWORK(1)` contains the reciprocal pivot growth factor norm(A)/norm(U). The "max absolute element" norm is used. If `RWORK(1)` is much less than 1, then the stability of the LU factorization of the (equilibrated) matrix A could be poor. This also means that the solution X, condition estimator `RCOND`, and forward error bound `FERR` could be unreliable. If factorization fails with $0<\mathrm{INFO} \le N$, then `RWORK(1)` contains the reciprocal pivot growth factor for the leading `INFO` columns of A.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (INFO)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "equilibrate", "factored", "not-factored"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `TypeError` eighteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `fact === "factored" && !( ( ( equed[ 0 ] === "row" \|\| equed[ 0 ] === "both" ) \|\| ( equed[ 0 ] === "column" \|\| equed[ 0 ] === "both" ) ) \|\| equed[ 0 ] === "none" )`)
- `RangeError` `RWORK` must have at least `max( 1, N )` elements from `offsetRWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, and i is \<= N:  U(i,i) is exactly zero.  The factorization has been completed, but the factor U is exactly singular, so the solution and error bounds could not be computed. `RCOND = 0` is returned. = N+1: U is nonsingular, but `RCOND` is less than machine precision, meaning that the matrix is singular to working precision.  Nevertheless, the solution and error bounds are computed because there are a number of situations where the computed solution can be more accurate than the value of `RCOND` would suggest.

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import zgbsvx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zgbsvx';

// 3x3 tridiagonal system (KL=1, KU=1):
// A = [ 4  1  0 ]    b = [ 5 ]
//     [ 1  3  1 ]        [ 5 ]
//     [ 0  1  2 ]        [ 3 ]
// Solution: x = [1, 1, 1]

const rcond = new Float64Array( 1 );

const N = 3;
const KL = 1;
const KU = 1;
const nrhs = 1;
const nRows = KL + KU + 1;

// Band storage (KL+KU+1 = 3 rows, N = 3 columns):
// Row 0 (superdiag): [0, 1, 1]
// Row 1 (diagonal):  [4, 3, 2]
// Row 2 (subdiag):   [1, 1, 0]
const AB = new Complex128Array([
	0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0,  // row 0
	4, 0, 3, 0, 2, 0,  // row 1
	1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0   // row 2
]);

const AFB = new Complex128Array( ((2 * KL) + KU + 1) * N );
const IPIV = new Int32Array( N );
const r = new Float64Array( N );
const c = new Float64Array( N );
const B = new Complex128Array( [ 5, 0, 5, 0, 3, 0 ] );
const X = new Complex128Array( N );
const FERR = new Float64Array( nrhs );
const BERR = new Float64Array( nrhs );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 2 * N );
const RWORK = new Float64Array( N );

const equed = [ 'none' ];
const info = zgbsvx.strided( 'not-factored', 'no-transpose', N, KL, KU, nrhs, AB, 1, nRows, 0, AFB, 1, (2 * KL) + KU + 1, 0, IPIV, 1, 0, equed, r, 1, 0, c, 1, 0, B, 1, N, 0, X, 1, N, 0, rcond, FERR, 1, 0, BERR, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, RWORK, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info );
console.log( 'rcond:', rcond[ 0 ] );
console.log( 'rpvgrw:', RWORK[ 0 ] );
console.log( 'equed:', equed[ 0 ] );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZGBSVX`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZGBSVX uses the LU factorization to compute the solution to a complex system of linear equations $A \, X = B$, $A^T \, X = B$, or $A^H \, X = B$, where A is a band matrix of order N with `KL` subdiagonals and `KU` superdiagonals, and X and B are N-by-`NRHS` matrices.

Error bounds on the solution and a condition estimate are also provided.

</section>
